display.title: Asarah B'Teves: A Time to Be Sad, a Time to Grow
display.summary_short: Why we fast on Asarah B'Teves: the siege of Yerushalayim that led to the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash, and how remembering sad days helps us grow.
display.summary_long: A talk for the fast of Asarah B'Teves from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi begins with Shlomo HaMelech's teaching that there is a time for everything: a time to be joyful and, once in a while, a time to be sad, not to stay sad but to become better. On the tenth of Teves the armies of Nevuchadnetzar, king of Bavel, surrounded Yerushalayim and sealed its gates, and the people inside grew weak from hunger. After two and a half years the walls were breached on the seventeenth of Tammuz, and three weeks later, on Tisha B'Av, the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed. We remember these days to ask what caused them and to make sure they never happen again. As long as we learn Torah and keep its mitzvos, no power can harm us, for, as Dovid HaMelech wrote in Tehillim, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
display.lesson: We remember sad days to learn from them and improve; learning Torah and keeping mitzvos keeps us under Hashem's protection.
